To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a modified protein-spare fasting is an effective treatment for obesity, but a combination of nutritional therapy and behavior modification seems to be more effective.
the most promising effects have been those utilizing a behavioral approach.

1) the most promising results in the treatment of obesity have been obtained when a combination of nutritional and psychological/behavioral approaches is used; 2) the most promising approach is a combination of protein-sparing modified fast with behavioral therapy; and 3) this treatment is more effective when it is performed in an in-patient setting than when it is performed on an out-patient basis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a practical, cost-effective, and effective program of weight control in the obese patient.
the development of a multifactorial approach in the treatment of obesity.
the evaluation of the effect of multifactorial treatment of obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a multifactorial approach in obese patients, including a hypocaloric diet, a behavioural therapy, and, if necessary, pharmacological therapy, leads to a good long-term result in weight reduction and in improvement of cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors.
multifactorial therapy of obesity is the most promising way to obtain a long lasting weight reduction.
multifactorial therapy including dietetic measures and behavioral changes are the most effective treatment in the management of obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of protein-sparing fast and behavioral therapy is a safe and effective treatment for obese patients.
the best results in obesity are achieved by a combination of a hypocaloric diet, behavioural therapy and a long-term support of the patient.
a modified protein-spared hypocaloric diet combined with a behavioural therapy is an effective method for the management of obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to achieve significant and sustained weight loss with the help of a multidisciplinary team.
the combination of diet and behavior therapy is more likely to lead to sustained weight loss than diet alone.
the combination of a protein-sparing modified fast and a behavioral therapy is an efficient treatment for obesity.
